newsitem.title: USA: Cyprus Amax plans copper production hike.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Amax plans copper production hike.

text.p: Cyprus Amax Minerals, already set to increase copper production sharply this year, is looking to raise output further over the next two to three years at its low-cost South American mines.

Milton Ward, Cyprus' chairman, president and CEO, told an analysts teleconference Wednesday that expansion opportunities at El Abra, its majority-owned mine in Chile which entered commercial production on Dec 1, were now being looked at.
El Abra is 51 percent held by Cyprus, and 49 percent by Chile state copper giant Codelco.
"We are going to expand it. Our partners want to expand it. It's just a matter of getting the work done," Ward said, though he added it was taking more time than expected.
A 15 percent expansion at El Abra could be completed "without much capital."
Ward added, "I would hope that we are looking at 25 percent plus (of expanded output), but we have got to do the work. It's a matter of economics."
El Abra's output is set to reach 500 million lbs this year, helping to boost Cyprus' copper production by 65 percent in 1997 to a billion lbs from 768 million lbs in 1996.
Some 35 to 40 percent of Cyprus 1997 copper production will be from low-cost Latin American output, Ward said.
Overcapacity had already been designed into parts of El Abra's operation, with transportation and conveyor belt capacity more than currently needed.
"The first block that we will hit would be in the electrolytic facility, and that probably will be power if we go above a 25 percent expansion," Ward said.

Cyprus' Cerro Verde mine in Peru, expanded mid-1996, produced 105 million lbs last year and Ward said the company was working with Fluor Corp at how best to raise output, probably by 20 to 25 percent over a likely period of 18 to 24 months when it goes ahead.

Production costs at Cerro, which produced 31 million lbs in the fourth quarter, were in the mid-50 cents per lb range, Cyprus said. "We would expect to stay in that range depending on how expansion works, and maybe even improve on that," Ward said.
Reserves at Cerro Verde will be expanded this year, Ward added.
Meanwhile production at the company's Arizona-based Tohono mine will remain suspended until an economic way can be found to develop it.
When operating, Tohono, which produced 38 million pounds last year, was adding some two cents a lb to Cyprus average copper cash costs, Cyprus said.
Fourth quarter net cash costs for copper of 70 cents a lb were five cents higher than in the 1995 quarter due to 10 cents a lb lower molybdenum by-product credits.
But when excluding by-product credits, there was an improvement of five cents per pound in copper cash costs due to lower cost production at El Abra and Cerro Verde.

The price protection program at El Abra ensures a minimum net average realization on an LME basis of 90 cents in 1997 on about 400 million lbs of the mine's output, with a cap of $1.25 per lb on about 145 million lbs.
